title: 亚马逊如何把办公地点的决定交给团队（2021）
topic: 亚马逊如何把办公地点的决定交给团队（2021）

source.title: Amazon offering teams more flexibility as we return to office
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 原文出自 Amazon 亚马逊 公开资料。
paragraphs: Subject: Updated guidance on where we work
I want to update you on how we’re continuing to evolve our thinking on where we work.

First, it’s worth reminding ourselves how challenging and unprecedented these past 20 months have been. We’ve never been through something like this before, and hope we never encounter it again. I’m appreciative and proud of how customer-focused and mission-driven the collective teams have been. It hasn’t been easy and not everything has gone perfectly, but the impact you’ve had on the lives of consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, creators, and brands in helping them cope with this discontinuity has been remarkable.

As we start to think about the future, we’ve all been asking questions like, “When are we really going back to the office, what will that really be like, how will I allocate my time between the office and home, how will others do it, do we need to be working in person together every day to collaborate and invent best, and how do we build connections and culture best?” We’ve shared a couple of updates on this topic, first thinking we’d be back in the office in September 2021, and then by January 2022, with the suggestion that we should all try to be in the office at least three days a week. This guidance prompted questions, like, “Who decides which days, does the team need to be in the same days, are there certain functions or teams that can work more effectively at home vs the office (and vice versa),” and many more. We met several times as a leadership team to discuss these questions, and generally agreed on three things.
translations: 主题：关于我们工作地点的更新指导
我想向大家介绍，我们对工作地点的想法还在不断演进。
首先，回想过去 20 个月，我们经历了多么艰难且前所未有的时期。我们从未经历过这样的情况，也希望不必再经历。我很感谢并自豪地看到，各团队始终以顾客为中心、以使命为导向。一路并不容易，也不是事事尽如人意；但大家帮助消费者、卖家、开发者、企业、创作者和品牌应对这场剧变，所产生的影响令人瞩目。

当我们开始思考未来时，我们都在问诸如'我们什么时候真正回到办公室，那会是什么样子，我如何在办公室和家庭之间分配时间，其他人会怎么做，我们是否需要每天一起在办公室工作才能最好地协作和创新，以及我们如何最好地建立联系和文化'之类的问题。我们已就此分享了几次更新，最初以为我们会在2021年9月回到办公室，然后是2022年1月，并建议我们都应该尝试每周至少在办公室工作三天。这一指导引发了诸如'谁来决定哪几天，团队是否需要在相同的日期在办公室，是否有某些职能或团队可以在家比在办公室更有效地工作（反之亦然）'等问题，还有更多。我们作为领导团队多次开会讨论这些问题，并大体上达成了一致意见。
fullTextParagraphs: Subject: Updated guidance on where we work
I want to update you on how we’re continuing to evolve our thinking on where we work.

First, it’s worth reminding ourselves how challenging and unprecedented these past 20 months have been. We’ve never been through something like this before, and hope we never encounter it again. I’m appreciative and proud of how customer-focused and mission-driven the collective teams have been. It hasn’t been easy and not everything has gone perfectly, but the impact you’ve had on the lives of consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, creators, and brands in helping them cope with this discontinuity has been remarkable.

As we start to think about the future, we’ve all been asking questions like, “When are we really going back to the office, what will that really be like, how will I allocate my time between the office and home, how will others do it, do we need to be working in person together every day to collaborate and invent best, and how do we build connections and culture best?” We’ve shared a couple of updates on this topic, first thinking we’d be back in the office in September 2021, and then by January 2022, with the suggestion that we should all try to be in the office at least three days a week. This guidance prompted questions, like, “Who decides which days, does the team need to be in the same days, are there certain functions or teams that can work more effectively at home vs the office (and vice versa),” and many more. We met several times as a leadership team to discuss these questions, and generally agreed on three things.

First, none of us know the definitive answers to these questions, especially long term. Second, at a company of our size, there is no one-size-fits-all approach for how every team works best. And third, we’re going to be in a stage of experimenting, learning, and adjusting for a while as we emerge from this pandemic. All of this led us to change course a bit.

For our corporate roles, instead of specifying that people work a baseline of three days a week in the office, we’re going to leave this decision up to individual teams. This decision will be made team by team at the Director level. We expect that there will be teams that continue working mostly remotely, others that will work some combination of remotely and in the office, and still others that will decide customers are best served having the team work mostly in the office. We’re intentionally not prescribing how many days or which days—this is for Directors to determine with their senior leaders and teams. The decisions should be guided by what will be most effective for our customers; and not surprisingly, we will all continue to be evaluated by how we deliver for customers, regardless of where the work is performed.

At this stage, we want most of our people close enough to their core team that they can easily travel to the office for a meeting within a day’s notice. We also know that many people have found the ability to work remotely from a different location for a few weeks at a time inspiring and reenergizing. We want to support this flexibility and will continue to offer those corporate employees, who can work effectively away from the office, the option to work up to four weeks per year fully remote from any location within your country of employment.

As almost all of you are hearing about this change for the first time, and will likely be eager to learn what your team’s plan is moving forward, I’d ask you to be patient with your leaders as it’ll likely take them a few weeks to develop and communicate their plan. We’re anticipating that you’ll hear from your leaders about these specific plans before January 3, which is the date we set previously for people to start returning to the office at least three days a week.

I also want to recognize our colleagues in Amazon’s fulfillment and transportation divisions whose roles aren't as flexible as most of our corporate roles. The work of these teams remains critical to communities around the world (and to the company's success), and the world has relied on them to deliver products to their doorsteps since the very beginning of the pandemic. There are other types of roles as well, such as those working in our AWS datacenters, physical stores, and those designing, developing, and testing new devices, who don’t have the flexibility to work remotely. I just want to thank these teammates for their passion, commitment, and continued dedication. It’s highly appreciated.

As mentioned earlier, these are unusual times and we’re all learning together what we believe is the best way to work together to make customers’ lives easier and better every day. And with it being so early in our mission, with lots of invention and change in front of us, you can bet that we will continue to adjust as we keep learning what makes most sense for our customers and teams.
Thank you for all your continued hard work.

scenario.title: Discuss who decides where a team works
english: A colleague asks what practical questions Amazon raised when it revisited its 2021 return-to-office guidance.
You summarize questions about who would choose office days, whether teammates should come in together, and which teams may work better remotely or in person.
You note that the email said there was no single answer for every team and that team-level decisions would follow.
chinese: 一位同事问，Amazon 在 2021 年重新讨论返岗安排时提出了哪些实际问题。
你概括了谁来决定到岗日、团队是否需要同日到办公室，以及哪些团队更适合远程或现场办公等问题。
你补充说明，邮件认为各团队情况不同，后续由团队层面作决定。

firstAttempt.prompt: 同事问 Amazon 2021 年返岗邮件为什么重新讨论每周至少到办公室三天的建议。请用英文说出邮件提出的两个实际问题。
firstAttempt.sample: The guidance raised questions about who would choose the office days and whether everyone on a team needed to be in on the same days. It also asked whether some teams work better from home or in the office.
firstAttempt.rationale: 回答只概括现有原文展示的具体问题，不补写后文没有出现在本课材料中的最终政策。

words.example: The company faced unprecedented challenges during the global pandemic.
words.translation: 公司在全球大流行期间面临了前所未有的挑战。
words.note: 用于形容历史上从未发生过的规模或情况

words.example: The market experienced significant discontinuity due to sudden regulatory changes.
words.translation: 由于突然的监管变化，市场经历了显著的中断。
words.note: 指事物连续性的中断或变化，常用于描述商业环境的变化

words.example: Teams across departments must collaborate effectively to achieve project goals.
words.translation: 跨部门团队必须有效协作以实现项目目标。
words.note: 强调不同团队或个人共同工作以达成共同目标

words.example: HR will provide guidance on the new remote work policy implementation.
words.translation: 人力资源部将提供关于新远程工作政策实施的指导。
words.note: 指提供方向性建议或政策，常用于组织内部

words.example: Managers need to allocate resources efficiently to meet quarterly targets.
words.translation: 经理需要有效分配资源以达成季度目标。
words.note: 指有计划地分配时间、资金或其他资源

words.example: Different business functions may require different approaches to remote work.
words.translation: 不同的业务职能可能需要不同的远程工作方法。
words.note: 指组织内的特定部门或职责范围

structure.original: I want to update you on how we’re continuing to evolve our thinking on where we work.
analysis: 主句结构：'I want to update you' 是主句，其中'I'是主语，'want'是谓语动词，'to update you'是不定式短语作宾语
介词短语作状语：'on how we're continuing to evolve our thinking on where we work'是介词'on'引导的介词短语，修饰动词'update'，说明更新的内容
从句结构：'how we're continuing to evolve our thinking on where we work'是由连词'how'引导的名词性从句，作介词'on的宾语，其中包含另一个嵌套的介词短语'on where we work'
structure.transfer: We are reviewing which work benefits from being together and which tasks can stay remote.

rewrite.bad: Amazon had already set one permanent schedule for every team and settled all questions about remote work.
rewrite.good: The email raised practical questions about who should choose office days, whether teammates should come in on the same days, and which work is better done at home or in the office.
rewrite.translation: 这封邮件提出了一些实际问题：谁来决定到岗日、团队成员是否应在同一天到办公室，以及哪些工作更适合在家或办公室完成。
rewrite.pattern: The message raised questions about [who decides], [how the team coordinates], and [which setting suits the work].

cloze.prompt: Which work would benefit from being together in the ___?
cloze.why: 先判断哪些协作需要面对面完成。
区分可以异步或远程完成的工作。

cloze.prompt: The team can decide whether shared office days would ___.
cloze.why: 由工作需要决定共同到岗日是否有价值。

dictation.text: Sarah, a project manager, needs to finalize the team's office arrangement for 2021, balancing between remote work and in-office collaboration.
The team has conflicting priorities: some members prefer full-time remote work for flexibility, while others value face-to-face interaction for better teamwork.

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否讨论哪些任务适合面对面协作？
translationPractice.answer: Could we discuss which tasks benefit from in-person collaboration?

translationPractice.prompt: 哪些任务可以远程完成？
translationPractice.answer: Which tasks can be done remotely?

translationPractice.prompt: 然后由团队决定共同到岗日是否有帮助。
translationPractice.answer: Then the team can decide whether shared office days would help.

choice.prompt: 同事问 Amazon 2021 年返岗邮件为什么重新讨论每周至少到办公室三天的建议。请用英文概括邮件提出的实际问题。
options: The email said headquarters would set one fixed schedule for every team and employees could not work from home.

The guidance raised questions about who would choose the office days and whether everyone on a team needed to be in on the same days. It also asked whether some teams work better from home or in the office.
The email announced a permanent rule that every employee must work remotely five days a week.
choice.why: 邮件提出的是讨论问题，不是已经确定的到岗规则。

output.prompt: 团队正在讨论是否安排共同到办公室的日子，但成员的工作内容不同。请用英文建议先了解哪些工作需要面对面协作，再由团队决定安排。
output.sample: Could we first discuss which work would benefit from being together in the office and which work can be done remotely? Then the team can decide whether shared office days would help.
check: 是否先提出了解团队实际工作的需要？
是否区分适合线下和远程完成的工作？
是否把安排交给团队讨论，而非假定一种方案适合所有人？
